name: Yellowish hazel
lede: Yellowish hazel is ColorHub's name for Nataneyu-iro, a Japanese color meaning "rapeseed-oil colored," and one of more than twenty ISCC-NBS names that fall in the same mustard-brown region.

sections.title: Rapeseed oil
sections.body:
菜種油色 (Nataneyu-iro) names the warm gold-brown of pressed rapeseed oil [1]. The same region of color is also filed by the ISCC-NBS system under names including Aurum, first recorded by Maerz and Paul in 1500, and Mastic, recorded in 1890, among more than twenty alternate names crowded into that one block [2].

The nearest look-alike is [[mustard-brown]], 3.1 units away and more vivid; [[bistre-brown]] follows at 3.5, almost the same [3].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The color appears in 2.12 percent of 23,781 paintings, 504 of them as photographed, more common than 78 percent of the names we track [4]. Fritz Thomsen used it most, in 4 of 18 works here, 6.2 times his museums' baseline [4]. The earliest dated match is a 1240 panel attributed to the Master of the Cross 434, though the archive's early centuries are thin enough that this is a floor, not a first [4]. It shares canvases with Poop Brown and Mustard far more than chance, at 15.2 and 13.2 times the expected rate [4]. As photographed, that lift is computed against the same museums' own baseline, not against painting in general [4].
